core: The working definition: the healthcare team as the group of professionals who work together on a patient's care (attributed as a working definition in the lesson)
The core roles: physicians, registered nurses, licensed practical nurses, nursing assistants, pharmacists, therapists, and social workers, one line each
Delegation: tasks move down the team with supervision; scope of practice as the regulated boundary (stated generally, per-state regulation acknowledged without specific legal claims)
Communication: handoffs and huddles as everyday team tools; AHRQ TeamSTEPPS framing that communication and teamwork skills optimize patient outcomes
Why teams matter: care is too complex for one person; the team is only as strong as its communication
supporting: AHRQ TeamSTEPPS program description (evidence-based teamwork tools; 2023 update; 3.0 curriculum modules: Communication, Team Leadership, Situation Monitoring, Mutual Support; patients and family caregivers included in the team)

claims.claim: For this lesson, a working definition: the healthcare team is the group of professionals who work together on a patient's care; AHRQ's TeamSTEPPS program describes teamwork as a set of tools used by healthcare teams, including patients and family caregivers, and MedlinePlus tells patients they can help prevent medical errors by being an active member of their health care team.

TeamSTEPPS is an evidence-based set of teamwork tools, aimed at optimizing patient outcomes by improving communication and teamwork skills among healthcare teams, including patients and family caregivers.

AHRQ updated TeamSTEPPS in 2023 to address changes in healthcare delivery and learning methods and to emphasize active patient involvement in their care; the TeamSTEPPS 3.0 curriculum is organized around modules on Communication, Team Leadership, Situation Monitoring, and Mutual Support.
Patients who are more involved with their care tend to get better results, and being an active member of the health care team helps prevent medical errors.
Registered nurses (RNs) provide and coordinate patient care and educate patients and the public about various health conditions.
Licensed practical nurses (LPNs) and licensed vocational nurses (LVNs) provide basic medical care.
Nursing assistants provide basic care and help patients with activities of daily living.

The healthcare occupational group includes technical and therapeutic allied health roles such as respiratory therapists, who care for patients who have trouble breathing, and medical assistants, who complete administrative and clinical tasks such as scheduling appointments and taking vital signs.

Delegation is how teams divide work: a task is passed to the team member whose scope includes it, usually from a more licensed role to a less licensed one, with the delegating professional retaining responsibility for the patient and supervising the task; scope of practice is regulated by state law and differs by state, so the lesson states the principle generally without asserting any specific state's rules.

A handoff is the structured transfer of a patient's information and responsibility between caregivers, and a huddle is a brief team check-in that aligns the team's picture before action; communication is a core teamwork skill in AHRQ's TeamSTEPPS curriculum (Module 1: Communication).

conflictingEvidence.issue: Who counts as a member of the healthcare team?
positions: Some descriptions treat the team as the licensed professionals only (physicians, nurses, therapists).
AHRQ's TeamSTEPPS explicitly includes patients and family caregivers in healthcare teams, and MedlinePlus frames the patient as an active member of their health care team.
conflictingEvidence.resolution: The lesson uses the inclusive framing: the team is the professionals who work together on a patient's care, with the patient and family caregivers included as team members per AHRQ and MedlinePlus.

conflictingEvidence.issue: Are delegation and scope-of-practice rules uniform?
positions: Delegation practice varies by state, setting, and employer policy; there is no single national rulebook.
The general principle — tasks move to a member whose scope includes them, with supervision and retained responsibility — is consistent across settings.
conflictingEvidence.resolution: The lesson states the general principle and explicitly notes that scope boundaries are set by state law and differ by state; no specific statutory claims are made.
